metadata.note: The West Shore Railroad (New York, West Shore and Buffalo Railway) ran along the west bank of the Hudson River from Weehawken, NJ (opposite New York City) north to Albany and on to Buffalo, competing directly with the New York Central's own east-bank main line -- until the Central bought it. Passenger service ran 1883-1958/59. Station order Albany-Weehawken: Albany (Union Station, Broadway and Steuben), Kenwood Junction, Ravena, Coxsackie, Catskill, Saugerties, Kingston, Highland, Marlboro, Newburgh, Cornwall, West Point, Haverstraw, Congers, West Nyack, Orangeburg, Tappan, and on into New Jersey (Northvale, Norwood, Closter, Tenafly, Englewood, Ridgefield Park, etc.) to Weehawken Terminal. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap: much of the New York stretch (the CSX 'River Subdivision') is still active freight track today, and the Rockland County/New Jersey stretch south of West Nyack -- long abandoned -- is well preserved as the Joseph B. Clarke Rail-Trail and Erie Rail Trail. GEOMETRY RE-TRACED 2026-08-24: the route was previously station-to-station hop routing with 50 straight-line steps over 1.2 km (the longest 11.1 km); 5 remain, both where OpenStreetMap does not map the alignment continuously. COLOR SPLIT 2026-08-24: per the same-company-same-color rule, feature(s) whose ownership passed to the New York Central were split at the documented transfer date into a pre-NYC feature (original company color) and an NYC-colored feature (matching new_york_central.geojson's canonical color), sharing identical geometry, rather than coloring the whole multi-era line with the original company's color throughout.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Shore_Railroad (main line Weehawken NJ-Albany-Buffalo, ~428 miles total; passenger service Jersey City-Newburgh began June 1883, Kingston next, open to Albany by July 1883; New York Central bought the line; Weehawken Terminal reached 1886 via a new Bergen Hill tunnel; passenger service ended to Albany 1958 and to West Haverstraw 1959, ending NYC passenger service on the Hudson's west side; station list Ravena, Coxsackie, Catskill, Saugerties, Kingston, Highland, Marlboro, Newburgh, Cornwall, West Point, Haverstraw, Congers, West Nyack, Orangeburg, Tappan, Dumont, Teaneck, Bogota, Ridgefield Park)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API): railway=rail (CSX River Subdivision, still active) combined with railway=abandoned/disused tagging and named rail-trail tagging (Joseph B. Clarke Rail-Trail, Erie Rail Trail) for the full Albany-Ravena-Coxsackie-Catskill-Saugerties-Kingston-Highland-Marlboro-Newburgh-Cornwall-West Point-Haverstraw-Congers-West Nyack-Tappan-Weehawken corridor; routed via Dijkstra shortest path through a graph of real track/trail ways, with no straight-line fallbacks needed anywhere on the route.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: 4 straight-line hops remain (3.2 km, 2.3 km, 1.7 km, 1.6 km), where OpenStreetMap does not map the alignment continuously; in three of them the previous station waypoints were placed on the east-bank Hudson Line or on other railroads' track rather than on the West Shore, so the endpoints themselves are suspect. Passenger dates (1883-1958/59) come from the earlier research in this file; no timetable has been consulted, so headways and speeds are estimates. The West Shore's main line turned northwest at Ravena for Schenectady and Syracuse -- only the Albany branch is drawn here, and the junction arrangement at Ravena is not verified.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.speed_source: estimated: 1880s-1958 New York Central-operated main line along the Hudson's west bank; unsourced

segments.note: Built by the New York, West Shore and Buffalo Railway to compete with the New York Central's own east-bank line. Passenger service Jersey City-Newburgh began June 1883 (using the Pennsylvania Railroad's Jersey City station, since Weehawken Terminal and its new ferries were not yet ready); Kingston was the next stop opened, and the line was open to Albany by July 1883. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

properties.geometry_source: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass -- active track (CSX River Subdivision), abandoned and dismantled railway, and the rail-trails that occupy the lifted sections. Built in two passes: the 13.4-mile Albany-Ravena leg was traced end to end, and every remaining straight-line hop over 1.2 km was then routed individually between its endpoints, accepting a result only if the traced path was no more than about 2.2x the straight-line distance. ALBANY END CORRECTED 2026-08-24: the line previously began with a 5.16 km straight line from a terminus placed at State Street and Eagle Street -- up the hill in downtown Albany, where no steam railroad terminated -- and its next several km followed the Normans Kill corridor rather than the West Shore's approach. It now runs north from Ravena through Kenwood Junction up the west bank to Albany Union Station at Broadway and Steuben Street, where West Shore trains actually terminated.
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, 1974 points, median vertex spacing 51 m, 90th percentile 313 m. Straight-line hops over 1.2 km reduced from 50 to 4 (3.2 km, 2.3 km, 1.7 km, 1.6 km), totalling 8.8 km of the 251 km route. Those four are where the corridor is not continuously routable in OpenStreetMap: two short breaks in the River Subdivision near Catskill, one near Newburgh, and the final approach to Weehawken, where the old waypoints sat on other railroads' track. Everything else is real traced right-of-way. Traced 156.0 mi; no company mileage has been checked against it. LATER ALIGNMENT: drawn on the corridor as it survives today, active track and rail-trail alike, not a verified 1880s alignment.

properties.speed_source: estimated: 1880s-1958 New York Central-operated main line along the Hudson's west bank; unsourced

segments.note: The New York Central bought the financially struggling line and, by 1886, operations extended to the newly built Weehawken Terminal via a tunnel under Bergen Hill. Operated thereafter as the New York Central's West Shore main line along the Hudson's west bank, competing with (and complementing) the Central's own east-bank Hudson Division. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
